_comment: Each entry mutates the fixture so that code and published spec disagree. 'expect' is the ground truth: what a correct auditor must report. Entries with expect:[] are decoys - refactors that change code without creating drift; a finding on one is a false positive. Literal string replace, not regex, so edits are exact and reviewable.

mutations.description: Payout fee field renamed in code; spec still advertises 'fee'. A partner reading fee off the response gets undefined.
Customer creation returns 200 in code but spec documents 201. Clients branching on status break.
A payout cancellation endpoint exists in code and is entirely absent from the published spec.
Spec documents GET /banks but the route is no longer registered. Integrators build against an endpoint that 404s.

mutations.description: Balance switched from decimal string to float64. Spec still says string. Float money loses precision and the type change silently breaks parsers.
Refund now rejects an empty reason, but the spec does not mark reason required. Every compliant client gets a 400.
Pagination param read as per_page in code, documented as perPage. Silently falls back to the default, so partners page through the same results forever.
Bank list now requires an API key; spec documents it as public. Unauthenticated clients that worked yesterday get 401.
